title: Exact recovery from rounded Fourier estimates
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, $k\in\mathbb N$, and $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$. Suppose the function on $\mathbb F_2^n$ obtained by identifying each binary coordinate with its corresponding sign has at most $2^{k+1}$ nonzero Fourier coefficients. Let $\mathcal F$ be a family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ containing every $U$ whose Fourier coefficient for $f$ has magnitude at least the threshold of the exact sparse-spectrum Goldreich–Levin input with parameters $n,k$. Form the sparse Fourier hypothesis on $\mathcal F$ from the empirical Fourier estimates of $f$ on the deterministic samples specified by that input, and round each coefficient to granularity $2(1/2)^{k+1}$. The sign-valued function obtained by assigning $+1$ to nonnegative hypothesis values and $-1$ to negative values is equal to $f$ at every point of $\{\pm1\}^n$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
the transported function on $\mathbb F_2^n$ has Fourier sparsity at most $2^{k+1}$
$\mathcal F$ is a finite family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$
every subset with Fourier coefficient magnitude at least the specified threshold belongs to $\mathcal F$
